# 📚 Top 5 Papers on LLM-Based Vulnerability Discovery for IoT Devices (2025–2026)

## Insertion Results

I checked the database and found a total of **5 papers**. Of these:

- ✅ **3 new papers were inserted** (IDs 57, 58, 59)
- ✅ **2 papers already existed** (IDs 23, 24 — PANGOLIN & ChatHTTPFuzz)

---

## 📋 Paper Summaries

### 1️⃣ FirmAgent: Leveraging Fuzzing to Assist LLM Agents with IoT Firmware Vulnerability Discovery
- **Venue:** NDSS 2026 | **Code:** [GitHub](https://github.com/vul337/FirmAgent)
- **Approach:** Hybrid — uses fuzzing to identify taint source points, then LLM agents perform context-aware taint propagation and automatic PoC generation
- **Results:** 182 vulnerabilities (91% precision), 140 zero-days, 17 CVEs across 14 router firmware

### 2️⃣ PANGOLIN: Fuzzing Multilingual IoT Firmware with LLM-Driven Code Analysis *(Already existed)*
- **Venue:** USENIX Security 2026
- **Approach:** LLM-driven cross-language code analysis (C, Python, Lua) with Multilingual Call Graphs and response-driven feedback
- **Results:** 68 zero-days (2.96× more than SOTA), 31 vulnerability IDs, 45 found in hidden interfaces

### 3️⃣ IoTBec: Recurring Vulnerability Detection for Black Box IoT Devices
- **Venue:** NDSS 2026
- **Approach:** Firmware-independent Vulnerability Interface Signature (VIS) matching + LLM-driven mutation fuzzing
- **Results:** 183 vulnerabilities (100% precision, 93.37% recall), 169 CVE IDs, 53 new ones (avg CVSS 8.61)

### 4️⃣ ChatHTTPFuzz: LLM-Assisted IoT HTTP Fuzzing *(Already existed)*
- **Venue:** Springer Int'l Journal of Machine Learning and Cybernetics, 2025
- **Approach:** LLM-guided HTTP protocol annotation, seed template enrichment, and dual-factor Thompson sampling
- **Results:** 103 vulnerabilities, 13× more than Boofuzz, zero false-negative rate in parameter annotation

### 5️⃣ Energy-Efficient Multi-LLM Reasoning for Binary-Free Zero-Day Detection
- **Venue:** arXiv:2512.19945, Dec 2025
- **Approach:** Tri-LLM (LLaMA + DeepSeek + GPT-4o) with energy-aware symbolic load model — no binary/firmware access needed
- **Results:** Simulation shows 20–35% higher zero-day likelihood under high exposure conditions; formal mathematical proofs

---

## 🧠 Key Takeaways

| Category | Papers | Core Innovation |
|---|---|---|
| **Hybrid Fuzzing + LLM Static Analysis** | FirmAgent, PANGOLIN | Dynamic fuzzing pinpoints entry points; LLM reasons about code paths |
| **Black-Box LLM-Driven Fuzzing** | IoTBec, ChatHTTPFuzz | No firmware/code needed — works on live devices via HTTP |
| **Binary-Free Detection** | Multi-LLM | Works with zero binary access using only system descriptors |

**2025–2026 is a breakout period** — 3 top-4 security conference papers (NDSS, USENIX) on this topic, with precision rates hitting 91–100% and hundreds of CVEs discovered.
